summary: The change passes. It fixes the cause where it starts. `PrLink` gains a defaulted `base_jobs` field. `land_pr` fills it in through `record_bases`: the other jobs whose open link head is an ancestor of this job's landing commit. After the job's own pull request merges, `close_carried_prs` in landing.rs walks `base_jobs`, and each earlier link's own `base_jobs`, and closes each earlier pull request with a comment naming the merging one. It closes a pull request only if the host reports it open and its current head is an ancestor of the merged commit or of the merged head (the second test covers squash merges). Pull requests that are merged, closed, partly carried or whose head git cannot place are left open. Every failure becomes a warning and the landing still stands. I ran the 14 new `stacked` tests and the 12 `pr::tests`, and all passed. Between them they cover the merge-commit and squash cases, the real-git three-job chain, the walk through earlier links' own bases, the shapes left open, the three failure modes, the retry after a failed close, and the client's REST calls. Athena's recorded CI run shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and docs/records.md describe the field and the rule. Four minor findings remain. (1) A merge first seen through `confirm_existing_merge` does not close the earlier pull requests. (2) The new close and comment write calls are logged under the read-pr host operation. (3) Several changed files are outside the expected deliverables list, though each is a one-line struct-literal fix the compiler requires, or a doc that criterion 7 requires. (4) The "fails without the fix" runs only showed the tests failing to compile.
